# Handoff

Capture everything a fresh session needs to continue this work, so the current
session can be ended without losing ground.

**Why this exists.** Every turn re-reads the entire accumulated prefix, so cost
per turn climbs with session length — measured at ~26K cache-read tokens per
turn in short sessions versus ~109K past 100 turns. Ending a long session at a
clean boundary and restarting with a handoff is the largest available
efficiency lever. The handoff is what makes ending cheap.

## Where to write it

```
~/.claude/handoffs/<cwd-with-slashes-as-dashes>.md
```

For example, `/Users/rashford/Developer/kitsune` →
`~/.claude/handoffs/-Users-rashford-Developer-kitsune.md`

Overwrite any existing file for this directory — the newest handoff wins. The
`SessionStart` hook loads it automatically in the next session, so **do not**
paste the contents back into chat.

## What to write

Aim for something a competent stranger could act on. Be concrete: real paths,
real command names, real decisions. Skip anything reconstructible from the repo
or from `git log` — those are already available to the next session.

```markdown
# Handoff — <one-line description of the work>
Written: <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM> · Session: <turns> turns

## Where things stand
Two or three sentences. What was being worked on and what state it is in
right now — not a history of the session.

## Decisions made (and why)
Only decisions that would otherwise be re-litigated. Include the reasoning,
because the reasoning is the part that gets lost.

## Files touched
- `path/to/file` — what changed and why

## What's verified vs assumed
Explicit. If tests ran, say so and give the result. If something was assumed
and never checked, say that too — this is the section that prevents the next
session from building on sand.

## Next step
The single next action, stated concretely. Then anything queued behind it.

## Open questions
Things the user needs to decide, or that were left unresolved.

## The confirmation handshake

Every mutating tool takes an optional `confirm` argument. Call it once **without**
`confirm` and nothing is sent to the controller — you get back a plan describing
the exact effect, the exact request body, and a token. Call it again with
identical arguments plus that token to execute.

The token is `sha256(operation | target | canonical_json(payload))[:12]`. Change
any argument that feeds the payload and the token stops matching, so a token
issued for one change cannot be replayed against a different one. This is a
**guard rail, not a security boundary** — a model could compute it in principle;
the point is that it cannot do so *accidentally*.

`target` is usually the bare object name, but it is not required to be. Where an
argument reaches the controller in the **URL path** rather than the body, it is
in neither the payload nor the object name, and folding it into `target` is the
only thing that binds the token to it. `nv_update_user_role` is the case that
matters: its `role` travels in the path, so its target is
`"<fullname> role=<role>"`, not `"<fullname>"`. Without that, a token previewed
for `role="reader"` would also authorise `role="admin"` — the handshake would
fail to gate the single field the tool exists to change. The controller call and
the request body are untouched by this; only the hashed target differs. Keep this
in mind when adding any mutating tool with path parameters.

### What `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` does not cover

`NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` is deliberately absent from the five layers above. It is
a **narrowing hint, not a boundary**, and it is fail-open by construction: the
check runs only when the tool can name the namespace its change lands in.

Of the 67 mutating call paths, **18 name a namespace and are checked**; the
other 49 pass none and are unaffected by the setting. The uncovered set is not
an oversight — most of those writes have no namespace to name:

- **Genuinely cluster-wide objects.** Registries, sigstore roots and verifiers,
  webhooks, DLP and WAF *sensors*, system and scan config, admission rules,
  compliance profiles. These exist once per cluster.
- **All of `iam_write`.** Users, roles and API keys are cluster identities.
- **Writes addressed by opaque id.** A network rule id, a response rule id or a
  packet-capture id carries no namespace, and resolving one would cost a read
  per call that the guard deliberately does not make.

So `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES=prod` stops a group, workload or service write landing
in `staging`. It does **not** stop `nv_delete_registry`, `nv_create_api_key` or
`nv_update_system_config`. Use `NV_TOOLSETS` to remove the toolsets a client has
no business calling, and provision the API key's NeuVector role to match — those
are the controls that hold.

landed, on both dimensions, including with the other dimension already

- verify_applied() replaces the single read-back with a bounded retry

only the compliance toolset reached GET /v1/user, and
nv_delete_group("../api_key/mcp-writer") issued DELETE

Fixed centrally with one validate_path() call at the top of
NeuVectorClient.request rather than by editing 63 f-strings -- a
central reject closes traversal and ?/# injection in one file with no
risk of a bad mechanical edit. "/" stays legal because a registry image
id genuinely is a repository path; going up still needs "..", which is
refused.

S1 (High) -- bearer scopes were decorative. nv:read/nv:write were
parsed, handed to StaticTokenVerifier and never read; an nv:read token
called nv_delete_group over real HTTP and the DELETE landed. Resolved
by removing the concept rather than enforcing it: privilege belongs to
the NeuVector API key's role, narrowed by NV_READ_ONLY, NV_TOOLSETS and
the confirm handshake. Two clients needing different power is two
Deployments. A legacy <token>:<scope> value is now a startup error, not
a silent strip -- stripping would preserve belief in a control that
never existed.

S9 (High) -- credential leak, found while fixing S1. Any Settings
validation failure rendered pydantic's input_value, i.e. the whole
settings dict, so a typo'd NV_TOOLSETS printed NV_API_SECRET_KEY and
NV_PASSWORD to stderr and on into the pod log. load_settings() now
re-raises ConfigError built from exc.errors(include_input=False) with

three times. The retry budget is now GET-only, with a retry= kwarg for
a caller that knows its write is idempotent. login() is unaffected, it
bypasses request().

P2 (Medium) -- re-login stampede. The 401 handler took _login_lock and
called login() with no double-check, so ten concurrent 401s produced

Secret fixed and verified.

## What changed on the cluster

- `Secret/neuvector-mcp-clients`, key `bearer-tokens`, patched with a JSON patch on that one key. Nothing else in the Secret was touched (it had no labels, no annotations, one key).
- **Value is now 64 chars, no colon, no comma, no whitespace.**
- **sha256 of the new value equals sha256 of the old 64-char prefix** (`2e2d6d823ab50aae`) — the token is byte-identical, only the suffix came off. Clients need no reconfiguration; the 64-char prefix is what they were already sending.

The handoff recorded the suffix as `:nv:read`. It was actually `:nv:read|nv:write` — same shape, and the `cut -d: -f1` approach still gave the right answer. Worth knowing there was exactly one entry: had there been a comma-separated second token, `cut` would have silently dropped it.

## The running pod is safe either way

The Secret reaches the pod as an env var via `secretKeyRef`, so the running pod (image `1.1.2`, 8 restarts, last 7h50m ago) still holds the old value in memory and is unaffected.

I checked whether the *next* restart would break it — **it won't**, and this is a code read rather than an executed test: `main`'s `config.py:212` does `entry.partition(":")`, so a colon-less token becomes the whole string with scopes defaulting to `["nv:read"]`. Since S1 established scopes were never read, that default is inert. The patched Secret is backward compatible with the deployed image.

I did not restart the pod. The fix was to unblock a future rollout, and a restart isn't needed for that.

The live NetworkPolicy still has the open ingress:

```
[{"ports":[{"port":8080,"protocol":"TCP"}]}]

My S5 change is committed in `deploy/deployment.yaml` but **not applied**. Applying it as-is would cut off any client that isn't in a namespace labelled `neuvector-mcp-client=true` — including anything reaching it from off-cluster. Before applying, we'd need to know what actually connects and either label its namespace or add the `ipBlock`.

Say the word and I'll find out what's talking to :8080 and apply it with the right selector.

**I broke external access for about a minute.** The live Service is a LoadBalancer, not the ClusterIP the repo assumed. Read by any skill that provisions, containerises, scripts, or deploys.

Companion files: `lab.md` (ash4d lab conventions and repo rules), `working.md`
(how to interact and what counts as verified).

## Containers

- **Images we author default to SUSE / openSUSE BCI base images.** Any
  deviation needs a stated justification and my authorisation before
  proceeding. Example of the rule applied correctly: `dli-power-mcp` builds on
  `registry.suse.com/bci/python`.
- **Pulling a maintained upstream image is not a deviation.** cloudflared,
  nut_exporter and similar vendor-maintained images get used directly — no
  flag, no authorisation request. The policy exists to keep our own build
  artifacts on a supported base, so wrapping someone else's binary in a BCI
  image to satisfy the letter of the rule buys nothing and creates a build path
  to own.

## Configuration management

**Salt is the preferred method for system administration.** A change that can be
expressed as a salt state should be, rather than a one-off SSH command or a
shell script copied to each host. Master is `pecan`; states and pillar live in
the `ash4d-salt` repo.

- **Salt owns the hosts.** Packages, files, services, users, OS-level config.
- **Fleet and `kubectl` own cluster workloads.** Salt manages the machine k3s
  runs on; Fleet manages what runs inside k3s. Keep that line — a salt state
  that applies a manifest puts two systems in charge of the same object.
- Prefer `state.apply` over `cmd.run`. `cmd.run` is permitted and deliberate —
  arbitrary execution at my request is the point of the open eauth ACL — but a
  change worth making twice belongs in a state file.
- Run `state.apply test=True` and show me the diff before applying. `state_verbose`
  is off, so a converged host prints nothing; output means drift, and the diff
  is the interesting part.
- Long operations go through the async API and poll the job. A synchronous call
  blocks until every minion returns and will time out on a real highstate.
- Every job is recorded in the master job cache with user, target, function and
  arguments. That record is the audit trail. Do not SSH to a host to do
  something salt could have done — it bypasses the record.
- Minion layout is not uniform. Package names, config paths and service names
  differ between stock `salt-minion` and the Uyuni Salt Bundle; branch on the
  `saltpath` grain rather than `os_family`. Which host runs which is state —
  it lives in Claude memory, not here.

## Languages

- **Python and Bash** for tooling, automation, harnesses and pipelines.
- Assume competence in Linux and Kubernetes; skip the primer and give me the
  command.

## Git

### Writing into a repo

- **Never Write or Edit into a repo containing `.entire/` from a Cowork
  session.** This covers new files, not only edits, and applies whether or not
  a commit follows. Check before *writing* — checking at commit time is the
  wrong gate and has already let bad writes through.
- Why: entire.io captures agent work through hooks
  (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`). Cowork
  does not run those hooks, so anything Cowork writes into the repo lands with
  no checkpoint lineage and the repo's provenance breaks silently.
- Instead: stage the artifacts to the session scratch dir or the mounted
  `_portfolio` folder, then hand me the file list and intended destination
  paths so I can run it through Claude Code in one step. If something genuinely
  must land immediately — a live incident — say so and get explicit
  authorisation first.
- Applying manifests to a cluster with `kubectl` is fine. It is repo *files*
  that are gated.
- Known entire-tracked repos are listed in `lab.md`.

### Committing

- Before any commit, verify `.entire/settings.json` exists and is correct. If
  it is missing, stop and tell me — do not commit. Never claim entire.io is
  enabled; it can only be verified, not enabled by you.
- Repositories that sync to **darthzen**: leave `.entire/settings.json` and the
  agent hook files committed, and let `entire/checkpoints/v1` push normally.
- Repositories that sync anywhere else: before the first commit, verify entire
  is configured with either `--skip-push-sessions` or
  `--checkpoint-remote github:darthzen/<repo>-checkpoints`. The
  `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch must never reach a remote I do not own. Do not
  stage `.entire/` or agent hook files into a pull request against that repo —
  use `entire enable --local` so the config stays in `settings.local.json`,
  which is gitignored.
- Commit only on my explicit instruction. I handle git.

## Secrets

- Credentials live in `~/Developer/keys/<service>/`, never in a doc, a
  preferences file, or a repo.
- Do not copy a token, key, or PAT into any file you create, including files in
  this folder. Reference where it lives instead.

## Working in a sandbox

- A sandboxed shell may be able to create files under `.git/` but not delete
  them, which strands `index.lock` and blocks every later git command. If a
  delete fails with "Operation not permitted", request delete permission for
  the folder rather than leaving the lock in place.
- Cloud-synced folders (iCloud, Dropbox) may hold files that exist only in the
  cloud. A shell command will error on those; reading the file downloads it
  first.
- The sandboxed shell and the file tools do not share a filesystem. Paths under
  the Claude application-support tree — memory files among them — are reachable
  by the file tools only.

# Base image policy: openSUSE / SUSE BCI only.
#
# SUSE BCI Python (SLE-based, SUSE-supported lifecycle) is the build and runtime
# base. The openSUSE equivalent, registry.opensuse.org/opensuse/bci/python, is
# the only other permitted base -- but as of 2026-07 its :3.13 manifest list
# publishes no linux/amd64 image (arm, arm64, ppc64le, riscv64 and s390x only),
# so swapping to it breaks the build on x86_64. Its :3.12 tag does carry amd64.
# No base outside those two is permitted here.
#
#   builder : creates a self-contained venv with pinned wheels
#   runtime  : copies the venv, drops privileges, no compilers on the final image

FROM registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13 AS builder

ENV PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \
    VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv \
    PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

WORKDIR /build
RUN python3 -m venv "$VIRTUAL_ENV"

# Dependency layer first so source edits do not invalidate the wheel cache.
COPY pyproject.toml README.md ./
COPY src ./src
RUN python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel \
 && python3 -m pip install .

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13 AS runtime

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="neuvector-mcp" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="MCP server for SUSE NeuVector" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="Apache-2.0" \
      org.opencontainers.image.base.name="registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13"

ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv \
    PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    NV_TRANSPORT=http \
    NV_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    NV_HTTP_PORT=8080 \
    NV_READ_ONLY=true \
    NV_LOG_FORMAT=json

COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv

# Fixed uid/gid so a PodSecurity "restricted" namespace can pin runAsUser.
RUN groupadd --gid 10001 nvmcp \
 && useradd  --uid 10001 --gid 10001 --home-dir /home/nvmcp --create-home --shell /sbin/nologin nvmcp \
 && chown -R 10001:10001 /opt/venv

USER 10001:10001
WORKDIR /home/nvmcp
EXPOSE 8080

# The server exposes no HTTP health path of its own; a TCP probe on the MCP port
# is the correct liveness signal. See deploy/deployment.yaml.
ENTRYPOINT ["neuvector-mcp"]
=== build-job (kaniko?) ===
# One-shot in-cluster build of neuvector-mcp 1.1.2.
#
# Runs on sdf1 (amd64) so no emulation is involved. The source is the public
# GitHub repo at main, cloned by kaniko itself, so nothing is uploaded from the
# laptop. The Harbor credentials are mounted straight from the existing
# harbor-pull secret and are never handled outside the cluster.
#
# Namespace is 'ai' rather than 'neuvector-mcp' because the latter enforces
# PodSecurity 'restricted', which kaniko cannot satisfy.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-build-1-1-2
  namespace: ai
  labels:
    app: neuvector-mcp
    role: build
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: neuvector-mcp
        role: build
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/hostname: sdf1
      containers:
        - name: kaniko
          image: gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.23.2
          args:
            - --context=git://github.com/darthzen/neuvector-mcp.git#refs/heads/main
            - --dockerfile=deploy/Dockerfile
            - --destination=registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/neuvector-mcp:1.1.2
            - --verbosity=info
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 2Gi
            limits:
              memory: 4Gi
          volumeMounts:
            - name: docker-config

Builds happen **in the cluster, not on the laptop**. A kaniko Job on sdf1 clones the public GitHub repo itself and pushes to Harbor. Nothing is uploaded from the workstation, and the Harbor credential never leaves the cluster.

## The shape of a build

```
bump version in the repo  ->  commit and push a ref  ->  kaniko Job clones that ref  ->  Harbor
```

kaniko clones from GitHub. **The bump must be pushed before the build runs**, or you get old code wearing a new tag. This is the single most common way to ship a wrong image.

## Fixed facts about this cluster

Verified against sdf1; re-check against the running system rather than trusting this list if something behaves oddly.

| Thing | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Build namespace | `ai` | Target namespaces enforce PodSecurity `restricted`, which kaniko cannot satisfy. `ai` does not. |
| Node | `sdf1` via `nodeSelector` | amd64, so no emulation. |
| Registry | `registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/` | Harbor. |
| Credential | Secret `harbor-pull` in `ai`, type `dockerconfigjson` | Mounted at `/kaniko/.docker` with key `.dockerconfigjson` renamed to `config.json`. Never handled outside the cluster. |
| kaniko | `gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.23.2` | |
| Cleanup | `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400` | The Job removes itself; no manual cleanup needed. |
| Typical duration | ~75s for a small Python service | Watch rather than assume. |

**Base image policy: SUSE / openSUSE BCI only** for images we author. Pulling a maintained vendor image (kaniko, skopeo, cloudflared) is not a deviation. As of 2026-07 `registry.opensuse.org/opensuse/bci/python:3.13` publishes no linux/amd64 image — its `:3.12` tag does — so `registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13` is the working choice on x86_64.

## Running a build

```bash
~/.claude/skills/lab-image-build/scripts/kaniko-build.sh \
  --repo darthzen/neuvector-mcp \
  --image neuvector-mcp \
  --tag 1.1.3 \
  --ref chore/release-1.1.3
```

`--ref` defaults to `main`. Pass a branch when the version bump is not merged yet — building from the release branch produces exactly the image main will have after a fast-forward merge, and it means the build is not gated on the merge.

The script renders the Job, applies it, watches to completion, prints the tail of the kaniko log, and then **independently verifies the tag in Harbor with skopeo**. It exits non-zero if any of that fails.

## Verify the push independently

kaniko printing `Pushed …@sha256:…` is the pusher's own account of events. Read the tag back:

```bash
kubectl -n ai run harbor-check --rm -i --restart=Never \
  --image=quay.io/skopeo/stable:latest \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"harbor-check","image":"quay.io/skopeo/stable:latest","command":["skopeo","inspect","--authfile=/auth/config.json","docker://registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/<image>:<tag>"],"volumeMounts":[{"name":"dc","mountPath":"/auth"}]}],"volumes":[{"name":"dc","secret":{"secretName":"harbor-pull","items":[{"key":".dockerconfigjson","path":"config.json"}]}}]}}'
```

The digest it reports must equal the one kaniko logged.

**Use `--authfile` with an explicit path.** Mounting the secret at `/root/.docker` and relying on skopeo's default lookup returns `unauthorized: … action: pull`, which reads exactly like a broken credential and is not one. This has already cost one debugging detour.

## Bumping a version

Grep for the old version rather than editing a remembered list — the set of files drifts. For `neuvector-mcp` at 1.1.3 it was seven files:

```bash
grep -rn "<old>" --include="*.toml" --include="*.py" --include="*.yaml" \
                 --include="*.md" --include="Makefile" . \
  | grep -v ".venv\|uv.lock\|<vendored-spec-dir>\|build-plan"
```

Typical hits: `pyproject.toml`, `src/<pkg>/__init__.py`, the server's `SERVER_VERSION`, the `Makefile` default `TAG`, `deploy/deployment.yaml`, `deploy/build-job.yaml` (header, Job name **and** destination), and README examples.

The Job name embeds the version with dots as dashes (`neuvector-mcp-build-1-1-3`). A Job is immutable, so reusing a name against an existing object fails — the script deletes any same-named Job first.

Run the repo's own gate (`make verify` or equivalent) after the bump and before the build. A version bump is not behaviour-neutral if a test asserts the version.

- **`make` may resolve `python3` to a pyenv shim without the dev tools.** Run gates as `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify`.
- **A build from `main` when the bump is on a branch** silently ships old code under the new tag. Match `--ref` to where the bump actually is.
- **Building the image is not deploying it.** The Deployment still names the old tag until its manifest is updated and applied. Say which of those happened.

It does not roll out. Updating `deploy/deployment.yaml` and applying it is a separate, deliberate step — and on a cluster with Fleet, it belongs in git rather than in `kubectl`. Ask before deploying unless the user asked for a deploy.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build an ash4d lab image with an in-cluster kaniko Job and verify it in Harbor.
#
# kaniko clones the repo from GitHub itself, so whatever --ref names must already
# be pushed. Building from a stale ref is the usual way a wrong image ships.
set -euo pipefail

NS=ai
NODE=sdf1
REGISTRY=registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab
SECRET=harbor-pull
KANIKO=gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.23.2
SKOPEO=quay.io/skopeo/stable:latest
DOCKERFILE=deploy/Dockerfile
REF=main
TIMEOUT=900

usage() {
  cat <<'USAGE'
usage: kaniko-build.sh --repo <owner/name> --image <name> --tag <tag> [options]

  --repo        GitHub repo kaniko clones, e.g. darthzen/neuvector-mcp
  --image       image name under the Harbor project
  --tag         image tag, e.g. 1.1.3
  --ref         git ref to build (default: main). Use the release branch when
                the version bump is not merged yet.
  --dockerfile  path within the repo (default: deploy/Dockerfile)
  --namespace   build namespace (default: ai)
  --timeout     seconds to wait for the Job (default: 900)
  --no-verify   skip the skopeo read-back
USAGE
}

VERIFY=1
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) REPO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --image) IMAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --tag) TAG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dockerfile) DOCKERFILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --namespace) NS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --timeout) TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --no-verify) VERIFY=0; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; usage; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

: "${REPO:?--repo is required}"; : "${IMAGE:?--image is required}"; : "${TAG:?--tag is required}"

DEST="$REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$TAG"
JOB="$IMAGE-build-${TAG//./-}"

echo "repo      : $REPO@$REF"
echo "dockerfile: $DOCKERFILE"
echo "destination: $DEST"
echo "job       : $NS/$JOB"
echo

# A Job is immutable, so a same-named leftover has to go before apply.
kubectl -n "$NS" delete job "$JOB" --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null

kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null <<EOF
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: $JOB
  namespace: $NS
  labels: {app: $IMAGE, role: build}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: $IMAGE, role: build}
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/hostname: $NODE
      containers:
        - name: kaniko
          image: $KANIKO
          args:
            - --context=git://github.com/$REPO.git#refs/heads/$REF
            - --dockerfile=$DOCKERFILE
            - --destination=$DEST
            - --verbosity=info
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: "1", memory: 2Gi}
            limits: {memory: 4Gi}
          volumeMounts:
            - name: docker-config
              mountPath: /kaniko/.docker
      volumes:
        - name: docker-config
          secret:
            secretName: $SECRET
            items:
              - {key: .dockerconfigjson, path: config.json}
EOF
echo "job applied; watching (timeout ${TIMEOUT}s)"

elapsed=0
while [[ $elapsed -lt $TIMEOUT ]]; do
  sleep 10; elapsed=$((elapsed + 10))
  succeeded=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$JOB" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null || true)
  failed=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$JOB" -o jsonpath='{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '  [%4ds] succeeded=%s failed=%s\n' "$elapsed" "${succeeded:-0}" "${failed:-0}"
  [[ "${succeeded:-0}" == "1" ]] && break
  if [[ "${failed:-0}" != "0" && -n "${failed:-}" ]]; then
    echo; echo "BUILD FAILED - kaniko log:"; kubectl -n "$NS" logs "job/$JOB" 2>&1 | tail -40
    exit 1
  fi
done

if [[ "${succeeded:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
  echo "timed out after ${TIMEOUT}s; job left in place for inspection" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo; echo "--- kaniko tail ---"
kubectl -n "$NS" logs "job/$JOB" 2>&1 | tail -5
PUSHED_DIGEST=$(kubectl -n "$NS" logs "job/$JOB" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}' | tail -1 || true)

if [[ $VERIFY -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo; echo "verification skipped (--no-verify)"; exit 0
fi

# Read the tag back. kaniko saying it pushed is the pusher's own account.
# --authfile with an explicit path is required; skopeo's default lookup against
# a mounted /root/.docker returns a misleading 'unauthorized ... action: pull'.
echo; echo "--- verifying $DEST in Harbor ---"
CHECK="$IMAGE-verify-${TAG//./-}-$$"
OUT=$(kubectl -n "$NS" run "$CHECK" --rm -i --restart=Never --image="$SKOPEO" \
  --overrides="{\"spec\":{\"containers\":[{\"name\":\"$CHECK\",\"image\":\"$SKOPEO\",\"command\":[\"skopeo\",\"inspect\",\"--authfile=/auth/config.json\",\"docker://$DEST\"],\"volumeMounts\":[{\"name\":\"dc\",\"mountPath\":\"/auth\"}]}],\"volumes\":[{\"name\":\"dc\",\"secret\":{\"secretName\":\"$SECRET\",\"items\":[{\"key\":\".dockerconfigjson\",\"path\":\"config.json\"}]}}]}}" 2>&1) || true

REGISTRY_DIGEST=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -oE 'sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}' | head -1 || true)
if [[ -z "$REGISTRY_DIGEST" ]]; then
  echo "could not read the tag back from Harbor:" >&2
  printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | tail -10 >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "kaniko pushed  : ${PUSHED_DIGEST:-<not found in log>}"
echo "registry holds : $REGISTRY_DIGEST"
if [[ -n "$PUSHED_DIGEST" && "$PUSHED_DIGEST" != "$REGISTRY_DIGEST" ]]; then
  echo "DIGEST MISMATCH - the tag in Harbor is not what this build pushed" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo
echo "OK: $DEST is in Harbor at $REGISTRY_DIGEST"
